name: e25
source: Derived, not independently sourced: a 25% v/v anhydrous-ethanol / 75% v/v gasoline blend (v = 0.25), computed from this project's own data/fuels/gasoline.json (LHV 44.0 MJ/kg, AFR_s 14.5, density 747.5 kg/m^3) and data/fuels/ethanol.json (LHV 26.8 MJ/kg, AFR_s 9.0, density 794.0 kg/m^3; both ultimately Heywood 1988 Table 9.7) via ideal volume-additive mixing: rho = v*rho_e + (1-v)*rho_g = 759.125 kg/m^3; mass fraction w_e = v*rho_e/rho = 0.261485; LHV = w_e*LHV_e + (1-w_e)*LHV_g = 39,502,453 J/kg (mass-additive, heat of mixing neglected); AFR_s = w_e*AFR_e + (1-w_e)*AFR_g = 13.061831 (exact - stoichiometric air per kg of fuel is mass-additive regardless of mixing). Assumptions: ideal mixing (the small negative excess volume real ethanol-gasoline blends show is neglected), anhydrous ethanol (EN 15376 blending-component composition, not hydrous pump ethanol), and a nominal 25% v/v label composition (unlike E5/E10/E85 below, E25 has NO EU standard of its own - Brazil's gasolina C is the closest real-world analogue but is not the standard cited here; this file's 25% figure is a nominal label composition only, not a certified maximum or minimum). Range cross-check: E25 has no EU density standard to check against; 759.125 kg/m^3 sits between the EN 228 gasoline range (720.0-775.0) and the EN 15293 E85 range (755-800), consistent with it being a genuine intermediate blend.
